title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A, B are small categories, A^ and B^ their presheaf toposes, and (A×B)^ presheaves on the product. The external product L⊠M is (a,b) ↦ L(a)×M(b), and e_{A^}, e_{B^} are the terminal presheaves. The map p_B^∧ : A^ → (A×B)^ is L ↦ L⊠e_{B^}, i.e. pullback along the projection A×B → A. Symmetrically, p_A^∧(M) = e_{A^}⊠M.

Corollary (of a formula on the previous page computing Hom of external products):
- p_B^∧ commutes with internal Hom: Hom(L'⊠e, L⊠e) ≅ Hom(L',L)⊠e, and symmetrically for p_A^∧.
- Proof idea: take M' = M = e_{B^} in the general formula Hom(L'⊠M', L⊠M).
- Direct check: at (a,b), Hom(L'⊠e, L⊠e)(a,b) = Hom((h_a×L')⊠h_b, L⊠e). A map X(a')×Hom(b',b) → L(a') natural in b' is determined by its value at id_b, so this equals Hom(h_a×L', L) = Hom(L',L)(a).
- In topos-theoretic terms, the projection induces a locally connected (essential) geometric morphism, and its inverse image is cartesian closed.

Grothendieck then specialises to L' = e_{A^} and replaces M' by an arbitrary M. He asserts Hom(e⊠M, L⊠e) ≅ L⊠e, induced by the canonical arrow Q → Hom(P,Q) (constant maps, adjoint to the projection P×Q → Q), which exists in any cartesian closed category.

Notation: on the previous page, X^M denotes the exponential in (A×B)^ of X by p_A^∧(M). This is the simplicial-type cotensoring with B = Δ, used to form X^{Δ_n} and X^{Δ̇_n} and the matching maps X_n → (X^{Δ̇_n})_0 ×_{(Y^{Δ̇_n})_0} Y_n, as in a Reedy / Kan-fibration setup for 'closed models' on A^ × Δ. Identifying L with p_B^∧ L and M with p_A^∧ M, the page concludes L^M = L for L ∈ A^ and M ∈ B^: objects constant in the B-direction are invariant under cotensoring by B-presheaves. This is a lemma serving the computation of matching objects for constant (B-discrete) objects in the previous page's fibration analysis.
errors: The final claim L^M ≅ L (equivalently Hom(e⊠M, L⊠e) ≅ L⊠e via Q → Hom(P,Q)) is false for arbitrary M ∈ B^. At (a,b) one gets L(a)^{π0(h_b×M)}, where π0 is the set of components of the category of elements. So the canonical map is an isomorphism iff h_b×M is connected and nonempty for every b.
Counterexamples: B = point and M = a 2-element set gives L×L. M = ∅ gives the terminal object.

For B = Δ the condition holds iff M is a connected simplicial set. It holds for Δ_n and for Δ̇_n with n ≥ 2, but fails for Δ̇_1 (two points), which matters for the X^{Δ̇_n} matching objects on the previous page (there L^{Δ̇_1} = L×L).
The specialisation does not follow from the M' = M = e case just proved, since changing M' to a general M is not covered by it; the general formula needs this connectedness hypothesis.

ideas.what: Pullback along a product projection A×B → A commutes with internal Hom in presheaf categories
ideas.modern_name: Inverse image of a locally connected (essential) geometric morphism is cartesian closed / preserves exponentials
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard topos theory (e.g. Barr–Paré on molecular toposes; Johnstone, Sketches of an Elephant C3.3)
ideas.where_published: Related material on locally connected morphisms in SGA4 (Exp. IV); not this precise statement as far as known

ideas.what: External product L⊠M of presheaves and the formula for internal Hom between external products
ideas.modern_name: External tensor/product of presheaves; exponentials in a product of categories

ideas.what: Objects constant in the B-direction are invariant under cotensoring X^M by B-presheaves
ideas.modern_name: Constant simplicial objects are invariant under cotensoring with connected simplicial sets (L^K = L for K connected)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses A^ × Δ-type models, but this lemma is not identified there

deep.surprise_reason: Routine presheaf/topos lemma: a product projection gives an exponential-preserving pullback, and constant objects are invariant under cotensoring. It contains an overgeneralisation that needs a connectedness hypothesis on M. Nothing new for specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: the crossed-out start appears to be '[-M'⊠e_B-]' before 'M' = M = e_{B^}'. The intended statement is M' = M = e_{B^}.
'faisant L' = [-…-] e_{A^}': the deleted symbol is a struck-out letter, possibly 'e_A', rewritten as e_{A^}.
'— ce fonctoriel via les flèches canoniques' probably reads '— ceci fonctoriel via les flèches canoniques'. The struck word is 'fonctions'.
'[-avec produits-]' may be '[-pas produits-]'. It is struck out and does not affect the meaning.
'M : e_{A^}⊠M = p_A^∧(M)': the handwriting has p_A^∧ with an altered subscript, consistent with p_A^∧(M) = e⊠M. Likewise 'L ⊠ e_{B^} ≃ p_B^∧(L)'.
'L ∈ A^' is written as 'L ∈ Ob A^' (overwritten); similarly 'M ∈ Ob B^'.
